item.title: Correction · DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (parcel 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (parcel 8722063) identical geometry: one shared master-condominium-association land parcel covering the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). That made the two records' shapes overlap completely on the map, so a click anywhere in the shared area could open either record, and each record's own location map showed the wrong footprint. Both now use non-overlapping shapes built from real data: Chase Center is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' OpenStreetMap building outlines subtracted, and Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 is the union of those same two outlines. Harmonic Brewing's standalone taproom building, at the northeast edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206 per its DataSF business-registration address; the registry's geocode puts Harmonic Brewing, Miller & Lux and Cupcakin' at the same point, so it does not place any of them in a particular building), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208 per its registration address; its position inside the arena footprint is not established by the registry) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures, so Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new shape rather than tracked separately. Re-matching business registrations against the corrected shape turned up three more Thrive City registrations: Cupcakin' Bake Shop (Ste 200), 'Siren SF' (1 Warriors Way Unit 24, shown as Siren Cafe & Bar) and The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way). These are registrations at Chase Center addresses, not proof of open storefronts, and each has its own entry.

item.title: Correction · Blocks 18B/18C corrected. A secondhand report that UCSF's own June 2025 CAC presentation (campus map updated December 2024) renumbers this row of blocks was independently checked. The childcare-center identification is an on-the-ground read, not independently confirmed by any source checked at the time, and is flagged as such in the record. A September 2026 accuracy check found that the UCSF deck cited (Dec 2024 map) lists Block 18C among 'undeveloped parcels remaining' with 'Open Space (Near term: Childcare Center)', which does not by itself show an existing building; no source read gives the 727 Nelson Rising Lane address or a 2006 start. item.title: Correction · P23 and P24 corrected. On review, the unmapped land between the Chase Center roundabout and 499 Illinois St (19,181.78 sqm, containing both plan numbers) was split into three pieces by width and each was mapped precisely. Both are added with approximate boundaries; about 5,785 sqm of the original area (the plaza strip hugging both buildings, the narrow extension and both dropped strips) is deliberately left untracked pending further review.

item.title: Added · OCII's own Mission Bay Land Use Map (December 2019; North blocks N1-N7/NP1-5/X1, South blocks 1-45/P1-P27/X1-X4/41-43 series) was cross-checked block by block against everything already tracked. Five more buildings were found and added: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision (490 Illinois St, 12-story, ~$237M, opened 2020), 499 Illinois Street / Alexandria Center for Science and Technology (UCSF-occupied biotech building, 2008), 550 Terry A. Francois Boulevard (former Gap/Old Navy HQ, now OpenAI-leased), 1180 Fourth Street (150-unit affordable housing, 2015), and Rich Sorro Commons (150 Berry St, 100-unit family and HIV/AIDS housing, 2002). Several false leads were ruled out: 360 Berry St ('Mission Bay by Windsor') turned out to be a 99.6%-overlapping alternate name/footprint for the already-tracked Edgewater, not a separate building; a candidate 'UCSF Community Center Garage' near the Rutter Community Center was mostly (65%) the already-tracked Rutter building under a different OpenStreetMap tag, with the untagged remainder unidentifiable, so it was not added rather than mislabeled; Historic Fire Station #30, Mission Creek Senior (225 Berry St), the Mission Bay Parks Maintenance Facility and 400/410 China Basin St all fall 90-100% within already-tracked parcels (the Public Safety Building, the Mission Bay Branch Library's block, Mission Creek Park, and blklots 8719003/8719008). Two items left open earlier were re-checked: Owens Street Garage is confirmed not a separate feature (91% of its footprint overlaps the UCSF hospital shape); the Edwin M. Lee Apartments (1150 3rd St) remain unresolved, with no footprint separable from Venue's in the available data, and are still left out rather than guessed. One self-intersecting source polygon (490 Illinois St) was repaired with zero area change. A September 2026 accuracy check found that the '12-story' and former Gap/Old Navy HQ details were not checked against a readable source; the $237M cost and 2020 opening (SF YIMBY, Nov 2020), OpenAI's lease of 550 Terry A. Francois Blvd (MF America) and 1180 Fourth's 150 units (Mercy Housing) were. The Rich Sorro unit count is 100 per the developer's page, not the 101 first written here.

item.title: Correction · A second correction to the Mission Bay coverage claims, using a more rigorous method: city blocks were built from DataSF street geometry and, for every block touching the Mission Bay boundary, the share of its building-footprint area covered by a tracked record was computed. Of 58 blocks with at least 30% of their area inside the boundary, 33 have meaningful building coverage (more than 3% of block area built), and 9 of those 33 were under 50% tracked. All 9 were investigated. 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard's map shape had captured only 1 of the 3 DataSF footprint pieces for its building (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the ~8636 sq m building) and now uses all 3. 1401 Third Street (an office building, built 2009, about 222,000 sq ft, both per the Assessor roll; tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, built 2009; 469,726 sq ft per a Redfin listing, not a primary source) were added. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them, and are left undocumented rather than guessed, like the 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This method is more rigorous than the satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the two earlier checks.

item.title: Added · A check of plan blocks 7E/7W, prompted by a direct question about that block, found a previously untracked building on its own Assessor lot (blklot 8711227, recorded 2012): the Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House, 540 Mission Bay Blvd North, a 5-story, 80-room nonprofit free lodging house for families of children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, built 2016. item.title: Added · A question about why the map showed plan block 7E but not 7W led to a re-check of how accurately the plan drawing lines up with the real map this far out. The alignment, fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core, drifts enough here that the 7W label lands inside a different, adjacent block's building: 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit and a mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats; SocketSite's Aug 2016 'about to break ground' item anticipated groundbreaking in 2016) that was not previously tracked. It was confirmed via its own Assessor parcel (blklot 8711505) and DataSF's Historical Secured Property Tax Roll. DataSF's Building Footprints layer captures only small roof-edge fragments of this building (confirmed against satellite imagery), so the record uses the Assessor parcel boundary instead, as a parcel-backed record rather than an approximate trace. Plan-label positions this far from the control points cannot be trusted to identify which building a label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax roll), which is the caveat under which the alignment was adopted.
